title: Payday Super teething issues recognised
full_text:
The ATO has observed a significant number of operational errors arising since the introduction of Payday Super stemming from issues with the electronic service addresses (ESA) of SMSFs.
“Since Payday [Super] began, we actually, just in the month of July alone, saw 40,000 errors [with contributions] returned from funds to employers because they weren’t equipped and ready with [an] active ESA,” ATO SMSF branch director Kellie Grant told delegates at SMSF Trustee Empowerment Day 2026, co-hosted by smstrusteenews and the SMSF Association in Sydney recently.
To this end, Grant highlighted a potential issue that may be preventing an SMSF from receiving employer contributions.
“[Trustees need] to ensure [the SMSF’s] electronic service address is set up to receive contributions and it remains active. Some ESAs are just set up for rollovers, [but] you need one that’s set up to receive contributions,” she explained.
“And keep that yearly subscription up so it remains active [because] if it lapses, your employer will then be unable to send contributions to your fund via the required SuperStream messaging.”
Apart from these Payday Super teething errors currently occurring, she stipulated a number of other measures trustees should ensure are present in order to facilitate employer contributions in a seamless manner.
“Ensure your fund’s bank account details are current [and] speak with your financial institution about the account’s ability to receive real-time payments through the new payments platforms such as Osko,” she instructed.
“Monitor contributions as they are received by your fund.
“And keep the lodgement of your SMSF annual return up to date and that’s because if you’re more than two weeks late with your annual return, your compliance status of your fund on Super Fund Lookup will change to ‘regulation details removed’, which will [result in] potential challenges for employers then making contributions into your SMSF.”
author: Darin Tyson-Chan
heading: Superannuation and Investments
